name: Industrial electricity use and output
fields: industry including construction, value added (constant 2015 US$)

sources.publisher: United Nations Statistics Division, Energy Statistics Database

join: Match reporting economies with the same geographic coverage and the same publisher-labelled year. Some countries use fiscal years. Distinct UN reporting combinations and predecessor areas keep their own identifiers and electricity observations. Unmatched inputs remain available as levels. No interpolation or substitution of a successor country.
growth: For each measure, 100 × (end / start − 1). Both measures must be present at each selected endpoint, each start value must be positive and the end year must follow the start year. The mapped gap is industrial electricity-use growth minus industrial value-added growth, in percentage points.
indices: Each measure is 100 in the chosen start year. Each later point requires both source values in that year. Exact source levels remain available even when only one is published.
interpretation: UN electricity consumption covers manufacturing, construction and non-fuel mining. Energy-industry own use and transport are recorded separately. World Bank industrial value added also includes fuel extraction and utilities. A difference in growth rates describes two related series with different activity coverage.
units: 1,000 million kWh = 1 TWh. Electricity-use footnote 1 denotes a UN estimate. An empty footnote alongside a numeric observation means the source supplied no estimate flag.
